timeline_reviews.summary: Reviewed the transport-level parent trajectory projection and used it to confirm run completion and final-response placement.
Reviewed the parent session: it spawned helpers, probed CLI behavior, wrote the hierarchical final graph, found extra child-created files, deleted them, reverified, and finalized.
Reviewed the probe_cli child session: it probed CLI and currency behavior, wrote a flat alternative implementation, spawned a review child, and returned a final noting extra files.
Reviewed the probe_numeric child session: it probed numeric behavior, spawned a nested CLI probe, wrote another flat alternative implementation, verified it, and was later interrupted.
Reviewed the nested CLI probe: it returned argparse findings to probe_numeric, especially around help, abbreviations, duplicate options, and missing-value behavior.
Reviewed the nested review_output child: it inspected the then-current output tree, found an invalid-currency mismatch in one intermediate graph, and was interrupted before final return.

direct_file_reviews.summary: Reviewed the same Python source, ESM .mjs requirement, manual argv parsing requirement, local-import-only constraint, and executable-probing instructions.
Reviewed aggregate metadata showing serial control mode, no subagents, no serial-control violation, and a 120/120 quality aggregate.
Reviewed current completed official status; it confirms serial mode, no child activity, artifact files, and a completed 120/120 evaluation.
Reviewed official evaluator summary; it confirms solution_passed true with 120 passed of 120 expected cases.

Reviewed the sole serial session: it probed executable behavior, wrote one coherent module tree, patched special-float parsing, reran comparisons, and finalized.

parallel.requirements: The parallel attempt recognized the pure Node.js ESM requirement, .mjs suffixes, manual process.argv parsing, local imports only, no Python or external packages, and black-box parity with the executable.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept main implementation ownership while spawning helpers for CLI and numeric probing; helpers also wrote their own implementation graphs, creating overlapping ownership of the same deliverable behavior.
parallel.implementation: The parent ultimately produced a hierarchical graph under lib/cli, lib/float, lib/decimal, lib/money, lib/program, and test6.mjs; child branches separately produced flat lib/*.mjs alternatives.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent observed extra top-level .mjs files from the parallel exploration, deleted them, reran final checks, and delivered the hierarchical tree only.
parallel.verification: The parent probed many executable cases, ran Node sample and edge checks, compared broader cases, checked help/error paths, and the official evaluator later passed all 120 cases.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official-output defect remained, but two helper branches were interrupted after the parent already had a working final graph, and their alternate modules had to be removed as stray work.

serial.requirements: The serial attempt recognized the same ESM, .mjs, manual argv parsing, local-only imports, no Python, no external dependency, and executable-parity requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent owned the whole pipeline: executable probing, parser modeling, decimal and currency implementation, entrypoint assembly, and verification.
serial.implementation: The serial run built a coherent tree under lib/cli and lib/money plus test6.mjs, including currency validation, decimal formatting, Python-float normalization, and argparse-like behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The single agent patched files in place, fixed special-float parsing, left one final module graph, and delivered the resulting output tree.
serial.verification: The serial run compared samples, CLI errors, abbreviations, zero, scientific notation, nan, inf, and other edge cases; official evaluation also passed all 120 cases.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial final response noted invalid-currency tracebacks were not byte-for-byte identical, but the completed official evaluator still accepted the solution.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the required ESM .mjs output, manual argv parsing, local imports, and executable-observed Python behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same required migration surface and worked from the same prompt and executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement coverage difference at closure; both implemented enough to pass, though parallel reached this through multiple overlapping branches.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed probing into helper agents while the parent also implemented and owned final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had one owner for probing, implementation, patching, verification, and delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced overlapping implementation ownership across agents; serial had a single continuous ownership path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel helpers were not confined to a file namespace or interface contract, so they produced alternate module names and layouts for the same behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial defined and patched one local interface set inside its own module layout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lacked a strict cross-agent file-scope boundary, while serial had no cross-agent interface transfer.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent wrote the final hierarchical ESM graph while child branches wrote competing flat module graphs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote one coherent ESM graph and then patched special-float parsing in that same graph.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented the same behavior, but parallel created multiple implementation paths that later had to be reconciled.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: A CLI child returned findings, review/numeric children were interrupted near closure, and the parent did not depend on their final results to finish.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child-result lifecycle; the same agent consumed its own probes and fixes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had child result and interruption management, but the retained adverse effect is the already-materialized competing file tree, not a missing result.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel shared-state integration required cleanup: the parent saw child-created extra modules and deleted them before final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integration stayed within one module tree and did not require reconciling another actor's files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the material task-solving process difference: parallel produced competing shared-workspace implementation paths; serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified samples, help/error paths, broad comparisons, and final output after cleanup.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified samples and edge cases, patched special floats, and reran a broad comparison before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both gathered enough acceptance evidence to pass; parallel verification also served to confirm that cleanup left the final graph coherent.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used five subagents and substantially more tool/token activity; it interrupted two helper branches after the parent reached closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, finished its single flow, and did not have child cancellation or merge cleanup.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had extra coordination overhead but did not exhaust the official budget or lose outcome quality; serial closed with less coordination overhead.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations show no discordant outcome: both parallel and serial passed all 120 test cases. The concrete difference is process-level, not final correctness: parallel created and then cleaned competing implementation files from multiple agents, while serial stayed in one coherent implementation path.
parallel_contributors: The parallel parent completed a verified hierarchical module graph and cleaned child-created alternate modules before delivery.
serial_contributors: The serial agent completed one coherent module graph, patched a special-float defect, and verified the final behavior.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial explicitly notes invalid-currency tracebacks are not byte-for-byte identical, but the official evaluator still passed it.
Parallel had intermediate child implementations with different currency behavior, but the parent final graph passed after cleanup.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is an adverse parallel process consequence only

candidates.reason: The parent and helpers all performed implementation work; the issue was overlapping implementation scope, not a missing implementer.
The parent owned integration and performed cleanup before final verification, so integration was not ownerless.
The parent assembled and delivered the final test6.mjs plus library tree; final assembly had an owner.
The parent drove the end-to-end path through probing, implementation, cleanup, verification, and final response.
Executable probing preceded implementation, but it was not a single mandatory gate that blocked all productive capacity or caused unfinished work.
Investigation overlapped with helper activity and the parent completed normal implementation and verification, so no serial investigation phase created an adverse closure window.
The indispensable parent implementation path received enough capacity to finish and pass; no critical path was starved by auxiliary work.
The run used several helpers and more budget, but it did not exhaust the official budget or prevent final verification and delivery.
No single child scope is shown to have been too broad and to have left indispensable final work unfinished; later child interruption did not affect the passed final graph.
The available child behavior shows they knew the task, executable, output directory, ESM, parser, and numeric requirements; no known requirement omission caused unusable work.
The agents did lack a strict file-scope boundary, but the realized event was concrete competing workspace writes, which the taxonomy directs to the concurrent-write family.
No known finding or constraint is shown to disappear during transfer and cause repeated work or a wrong final action.
Child outputs were not shown to be too large or insufficiently structured for the parent to consume within the decision window.
No receiver acted on a superseded report or workspace state; the parent inspected current files and cleaned the final tree.
Although implementation outputs conflicted in file layout, there were not incompatible returned reports left unadjudicated; the concrete issue was the competing write set.
The parent ran integrated checks after cleanup and the official evaluation passed; no parent-visible unresolved acceptance gap remained at completion.
No replacement retry repeated prior work without inherited state; the run used helpers and patches, not a checkpoint-free retry cycle.

candidates.reason: Two helpers were interrupted, but only after the parent had implemented, cleaned, and verified a passing final graph; no needed child result was cut off.
A complete deliverable was finalized and verified before closure; the alternate child graphs were competing work, not a single promotable candidate left unplaced.
The parent performed verification after cleaning the output tree, so no child result or code merge occurred only after the relevant checks.
Completed child implementation work was not silently unjoined; the parent observed the extra files and reconciled them by removing the alternate graph.
The review child was interrupted and did not produce a final concrete verifier finding that was trapped below the parent before closure.
Interrupted helper work did not leave required scope unresolved; the parent had already taken over and completed the final implementation path.
The parent did not ignore a visible result and proceed inconsistently; it observed extra output files and explicitly removed the alternate modules.
The parent had timed waits, but it also inspected agents and workspace state and those waits did not cause missed required work.
Concurrent agents wrote different module layouts and implementation paths that all claimed the test6 CLI and Money-halving behavior, forcing parent reconciliation before delivery.
candidates.realized_consequence: The parent had to inspect the output tree and remove nine child-created alternate modules before final verification, discarding/reconciling overlapping branch work.
candidates.near_match_reason: The parent did delete child-created modules, but the defining problem was competing cross-file implementation scopes; no actively used final-graph source path was replaced by another source implementation.

The parent cleaned stray alternate modules but did not broadly replace another completed final tree or invalidate a selected final-tree provenance.
The workspace was shared, but a more specific cross-file scope collision is directly evidenced by competing implementation paths and cleanup.
No generated artifact, cache, fixture, process, or auxiliary implementation from one actor was consumed by another as a stable reference environment.
